chapters.title: The Italian Chains
chapters.intro: Where I grew up and where I can tell you everything they do wrong.

chapters.title: The Steakhouse & Grill
chapters.intro: You're paying $38 for a steak you can cook better tonight.

chapters.title: The Mexican Chains
chapters.intro: Rice, beans, salsa. Pennies. And they charge you $14.

chapters.title: The Asian Takeout
chapters.intro: Faster than delivery and you know what's in it.

chapters.title: The Fast Food & Diner Classics
chapters.intro: The stuff your grandkids beg for, made the right way.

chapters.title: Sal's Sauces
chapters.intro: The jars cost $8. These cost about $2 and taste like a real kitchen.

recipes.title: Garlic Butter Breadsticks
recipes.subtitle: Like the bottomless breadsticks at the big Italian chain
recipes.tip: The chains brush them twice. That second brush is why you can't stop eating them. Now you know.
ingredientNames: (1 packet) instant or active dry yeast
Topping: 4 tbsp melted butter, 1/2 tsp garlic powder, 1/2 tsp salt, pinch of dried oregano

recipes.title: Real Fettuccine Alfredo
recipes.subtitle: Like the alfredo every Italian chain puts on the menu
recipes.tip: Grate the cheese yourself. Pre-shredded cheese has anti-caking powder in it and your sauce will turn grainy.
ingredientNames: freshly grated Parmigiano-Reggiano (not the green can)
Salt, black pepper, pinch of nutmeg

recipes.title: Sausage, Potato & Kale Soup
recipes.subtitle: Like the creamy Tuscan soup at the Italian chain
recipes.tip: Slice the potatoes thin and even. Thick chunks make it a stew, thin slices make it the soup you remember.
ingredientNames: Italian sausage (mild or hot), casings removed

recipes.title: House Salad with Italian Dressing
recipes.subtitle: Like the never-ending salad at the Italian chain
recipes.tip: The mayonnaise is the secret. It makes the dressing creamy and stops it from separating.
ingredientNames: Dressing: 1/2 cup olive oil, 1/4 cup white wine vinegar, 2 tbsp mayonnaise, 2 tbsp grated parmesan, 1 tbsp water, 1 tsp sugar, 1 tsp Italian seasoning, 1/2 tsp garlic powder, 1/2 tsp salt, 1 tbsp lemon juice
Salad: 1 head iceberg lettuce and 1 heart of romaine, chopped

recipes.title: Chicken Parmigiana
recipes.subtitle: Like the chicken parm on every Italian-American menu in the country
recipes.tip: Put sauce on top only, never under the chicken. Sauce underneath makes the crust soggy, and that's how you know it was made by somebody who doesn't care.
ingredientNames: chicken breasts, halved horizontally into 4 cutlets
flour, 2 eggs beaten, 1 1/2 cups panko mixed with 1/2 cup grated parmesan

recipes.title: Shrimp Scampi
recipes.subtitle: Like the scampi at the Italian and seafood chains
recipes.tip: Take the shrimp out early. They finish cooking in the sauce. Rubber shrimp is the number one restaurant crime.

recipes.title: Angela's Tiramisu
recipes.subtitle: My wife made this every morning for 40 years. No box, no freezer.
recipes.tip: One second in the coffee. Angela would hit my hand if I counted to two.

recipes.title: Cheddar Garlic Biscuits
recipes.subtitle: Like the famous biscuits at the seafood chain
recipes.tip: Cold butter, quick hands. Warm butter gives you hockey pucks.
ingredientNames: Topping: 3 tbsp melted butter, 1/2 tsp garlic powder, 1 tsp dried parsley

recipes.title: Pan-Seared Steak with Garlic Butter
recipes.subtitle: Like the steakhouse sirloin, but better
recipes.tip: Salt early and get the pan hot. That's all a steakhouse does. Plus they charge you $38.
ingredientNames: steaks (sirloin, ribeye or strip), 1 to 1 1/4 inch thick

recipes.title: Loaded Baked Potato Soup
recipes.subtitle: Like the potato soup at the casual grill chains
recipes.tip: Mash half, leave half. Smooth and chunky at the same time, like a real baked potato.

recipes.title: Hot Spinach Artichoke Dip
recipes.subtitle: Like the dip every grill chain sells you as an appetizer
recipes.tip: Squeeze the spinach until your hands hurt. Wet spinach equals watery dip.
ingredientNames: frozen spinach, thawed and squeezed very dry
garlic, minced, pinch of red pepper flakes

recipes.title: Honey Butter Dinner Rolls
recipes.subtitle: Like the sweet rolls at the steakhouse chains
recipes.tip: Make a double batch of the honey butter. It keeps two weeks in the fridge and your grandkids will put it on everything.
ingredientNames: Honey butter: 1/2 cup soft butter, 3 tbsp honey, 1/4 tsp cinnamon, pinch of salt

recipes.title: Restaurant-Style Blender Salsa
recipes.subtitle: Like the free salsa at the Tex-Mex chains
recipes.tip: Canned tomatoes, not fresh. That's what most restaurants use, and that's why theirs tastes the same in January as in August.

recipes.title: Cilantro Lime Rice
recipes.subtitle: Like the rice at the fast-casual burrito chain
recipes.tip: The bay leaf is the thing nobody tells you about. Try it once without and you'll see.
ingredientNames: Juice of 1 large lime + 1 tsp zest

recipes.title: Sizzling Chicken Fajitas
recipes.subtitle: Like the fajitas that come out smoking at the Tex-Mex chains
recipes.tip: Thighs, not breasts. Restaurants use thighs because they stay juicy. You should too.
ingredientNames: chicken thighs or breasts, sliced into strips
Marinade: 3 tbsp oil, juice of 2 limes, 1 tbsp chili powder, 1 tsp cumin, 1 tsp smoked paprika, 1 tsp garlic powder, 1 tsp salt, 1 tsp sugar
To serve: sour cream, salsa, guacamole, cheese

recipes.title: White Queso Dip
recipes.subtitle: Like the queso at the Mexican restaurants
recipes.tip: Deli white American cheese is the secret. It melts smooth and never breaks. Don't be a snob about it.
ingredientNames: white American cheese from the deli, torn

recipes.title: Burrito Bowl at Home
recipes.subtitle: Like the build-your-own bowls at the burrito chain
recipes.tip: Chipotle in adobo comes in a little can for about two dollars. That smoky taste you love? That's the can.
ingredientNames: Marinade: 2 chipotle peppers in adobo + 2 tbsp of the sauce, 2 tbsp oil, 3 cloves garlic, 1 tsp cumin, 1 tsp oregano, 1 tsp salt
black beans, warmed with a pinch of cumin
Salsa, corn, cheese, lettuce, sour cream, guacamole

recipes.title: Orange Chicken
recipes.subtitle: Like the orange chicken at the mall food court chain
recipes.tip: Fry a second time for 1 minute just before saucing if you want it extra crispy. That's the restaurant way.
ingredientNames: egg, 1/2 cup cornstarch, 1/4 cup flour, salt

Sauce: 3/4 cup orange juice, zest of 1 orange, 1/3 cup sugar, 2 tbsp soy sauce, 2 tbsp rice vinegar, 2 cloves garlic, 1 tsp grated ginger, pinch of red pepper flakes, 1 tbsp cornstarch mixed with 2 tbsp water

recipes.title: Better Chow Mein
recipes.subtitle: Like the chow mein at the Chinese takeout chains
recipes.tip: Cabbage is the cheapest vegetable in the store and it's exactly what they use. Don't let anybody tell you it's fancy.
ingredientNames: fresh chow mein or lo mein noodles (or spaghetti)
Sauce: 3 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tbsp oyster sauce, 1 tsp sesame oil, 1 tsp sugar, 2 cloves garlic, 1 tsp grated ginger

recipes.title: Takeout Fried Rice
recipes.subtitle: Like the fried rice at every takeout place you've ever ordered from
recipes.tip: Cold rice. Always. Fresh rice turns to mush. Restaurants use yesterday's rice, and for once they're right.
ingredientNames: soy sauce, 1 tsp sesame oil, 1/2 tsp white pepper
Optional: diced ham, chicken or shrimp

recipes.title: Chicken Lettuce Wraps
recipes.subtitle: Like the lettuce wraps at the upscale Asian-fusion chain
recipes.tip: Water chestnuts give the crunch. Without them it's just chicken in a salad.
ingredientNames: Sauce: 3 tbsp hoisin, 2 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tbsp rice vinegar, 1 tsp sesame oil, 1 tsp sriracha

recipes.title: Smash Burgers with Special Sauce
recipes.subtitle: Like the burgers at the famous West Coast and East Coast burger chains
recipes.tip: Smash it in the first 10 seconds and never again. That crispy edge is the whole point.
ingredientNames: 80/20 ground beef, made into 8 loose balls
soft potato buns, toasted with butter
Sauce: 1/2 cup mayo, 2 tbsp ketchup, 1 tbsp sweet relish, 1 tsp mustard, 1 tsp white vinegar, pinch of sugar, salt and pepper

recipes.title: Crispy Chicken Sandwich
recipes.subtitle: Like the chicken sandwich everybody lines up for
recipes.tip: Pickle juice and a little powdered sugar. Now you know why it tastes the way it tastes.
ingredientNames: chicken breasts, halved into 4 thin cutlets
Brine: 1 cup pickle juice + 1/2 cup milk
Coating: 1 cup flour, 2 tbsp powdered sugar, 1 tsp paprika, 1 tsp salt, 1/2 tsp black pepper, 1/2 tsp garlic powder
Oil for frying, 4 buttered toasted buns, dill pickle chips

recipes.title: Classic Diner Chili
recipes.subtitle: Like the chili at the square-burger fast food chain
recipes.tip: It's better the next day. In my restaurant, chili was always yesterday's chili. That one's a good trick.
ingredientNames: onion, 1 green bell pepper, 2 celery stalks, all diced
chili powder, 1 tbsp cumin, 1 tsp oregano, 1 tsp paprika, 1 tsp sugar
diced tomatoes + 15 oz can tomato sauce
kidney beans and 1 can pinto beans, drained

recipes.title: Creamy Coleslaw
recipes.subtitle: Like the coleslaw at the fried chicken chain
recipes.tip: Chop it tiny. That's the difference between their slaw and the picnic slaw everybody leaves on the plate.
ingredientNames: very finely chopped cabbage (about 1 small head)
Dressing: 1/2 cup mayo, 1/3 cup sugar, 1/4 cup milk, 1/4 cup buttermilk, 2 1/2 tbsp lemon juice, 1 1/2 tbsp white vinegar, 1/2 tsp salt, 1/8 tsp pepper

recipes.title: Fluffy Diner Pancakes
recipes.subtitle: Like the stacks at the pancake house chains
recipes.tip: Rest the batter and don't stir it again. Ten minutes of waiting is what makes them tall.
ingredientNames: sugar, 2 tsp baking powder, 1/2 tsp baking soda, 1/2 tsp salt
melted butter + more for the pan

recipes.title: Baked Mac and Cheese
recipes.subtitle: Like the mac and cheese at the Southern-style chains
recipes.tip: Evaporated milk keeps it creamy even the next day. It's the oldest diner trick there is.
ingredientNames: mustard powder, 1/2 tsp paprika, salt and pepper
Topping: 1/2 cup panko with 1 tbsp melted butter

recipes.title: Oven-Baked Buffalo Wings
recipes.subtitle: Like the wings at the sports bar chains
recipes.tip: Baking powder pulls the moisture out of the skin. Crispy wings, no fryer. You're welcome.
ingredientNames: chicken wings, split, tips removed, patted very dry
baking powder (NOT baking soda), 1 tsp salt
Sauce: 1/2 cup hot sauce (cayenne type), 4 tbsp butter, 1 tsp garlic powder, 1 tsp Worcestershire
Blue cheese or ranch, celery sticks

recipes.title: Chocolate Lava Cakes
recipes.subtitle: Like the molten cake dessert at the casual dining chains
recipes.tip: You can fill the ramekins in the morning and bake them after dinner. That's exactly how the restaurant does it.
ingredientNames: Butter and cocoa for the ramekins

recipes.title: Sunday Marinara
recipes.subtitle: The sauce from Romano's. The base for half this book.
ingredients: Two 28 oz cans whole San Marzano- style tomatoes, crushed by hand
1 tsp salt, pinch of red pepper flakes, 1 tsp sugar (only if the tomatoes are sour)
steps: Cook the onion in the oil over medium-low heat 8 minutes until soft and sweet.
Add the garlic for 1 minute without browning.
Add the tomatoes, salt, pepper flakes and oregano.
Simmer gently 30 to 40 minutes, stirring now and then.
Tear in the basil at the end. Taste for salt.
recipes.tip: Low heat, patience. A burnt garlic sauce is a sauce you pour down the drain.

recipes.title: Garlic Butter Sauce
recipes.subtitle: The sauce for steak, shrimp, bread and everything else
ingredients: 2 tbsp chopped parsley, salt and pepper
steps: Melt the butter over medium-low heat.
Add the garlic and cook 1 to 2 minutes until fragrant, not brown.
Add the broth and lemon. Simmer 1 minute.
recipes.tip: Spoon it over a cheap sirloin and your family will think you went to the steakhouse.

recipes.title: Steak Sauce
recipes.subtitle: Like the brown bottled steak sauce, but fresh
recipes.tip: The raisins. That's the sweet-tangy thing you could never figure out.
ingredientNames: raisins, soaked in hot water 10 min

recipes.title: Buttermilk Ranch
recipes.subtitle: Like the ranch at the wing and pizza chains
ingredients: 1/2 tsp garlic powder, 1/2 tsp onion powder
1 tsp lemon juice, salt and pepper
steps: Thin with more buttermilk if you want it for salad, keep it thick for dipping.
Chill at least 1 hour. Keeps 5 days.
recipes.tip: Fresh herbs if you can. The bottle never tastes like this.
